hook: Paramecium sonneborni carries chromosome-sized DNA from species too distant to normally interbreed.
hook_turn: from species too distant to normally interbreed.
summary: Genome analysis of P. sonneborni found hundreds of segments, some near chromosome length, from very distant paramecium lineages, which points to repeated mating across species. The authors propose paramecia tolerate this because foreign DNA is stripped from the somatic nucleus. The mechanism is inferred from genome sequences, not tested by crossing.
title: Recurrent hybridization between highly divergent paramecium species.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
